types.name: Fenrir::AssetHandle<Fenrir::Skeleton>
types.doc: Names one asset of kind `T` (`Mesh`, `Image`, `Material`, `Shader`, `Model`, `Skeleton`, `Clip` or `BoneMask`) in the asset store: a slot index plus the generation the slot had when the asset was made (ADR-0021). Plain data that keeps nothing alive, so components hold it and C# receives it as a value. Once the asset is freed the slot's generation moves on and the handle is stale: it no longer resolves, and users skip it. A default-made handle is empty and never resolves.

types.name: Fenrir::AttachmentState
types.doc: Whether the last Attach placed a bone attachment's entity, and why not (ADR-0037).

values.name: NotAttached
values.doc: The entity has no `BoneAttachment`, or no Attach has seen it yet.

values.name: Attached
values.doc: Placed at its bone this frame.

values.name: SkeletonMissing
values.doc: The skeleton entity is dead, or has no `SkeletonPose`.

values.name: SkeletonUnavailable
values.doc: The skeleton entity's instance is `Unavailable`.

values.name: BoneNotFound
values.doc: No bone has that engine name, or the name is malformed.

values.name: TransformMissing
values.doc: The entity has no `Transform` to place.

values.name: Unplaceable
values.doc: The parent's world matrix has no inverse, or the attachment is in a dependency cycle.

types.name: Fenrir::BoneName
types.doc: A bone's engine name as a component field (ADR-0037): a fixed 256-byte UTF-8 buffer, like `Name`, holding at most 255 bytes and a terminator. `Set` refuses a longer name rather than truncating it, since a truncated name could match another bone. A buffer written raw with no terminator is malformed: `Get` gives nothing, and an attachment naming it is diagnosed and never resolved.

types.name: Fenrir::Entity
types.doc: Entity class that is used to interact with the entity list. This forms the basis of the ECS

types.name: Fenrir::Transform
types.doc: An entity's place in the world, relative to its parent: every entity has one.

fields.name: pos
fields.doc: The position, relative to the parent.

fields.name: rot
fields.doc: The rotation, relative to the parent.

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: The scale on each axis, relative to the parent.

types.name: Fenrir::BoneAttachment
types.doc:
A bone attachment (ADR-0037): plain data placing its entity at a bone of a skeleton entity every frame, at `GetBoneWorldMatrix(skeleton, bone) × offset`, under whatever ECS parent the entity has. The full bone transform is inherited, translation, rotation and scale.

While an entity has one, FenrirSkeleton owns its local `Transform`, written in the pose pipeline's Attach step: move the object relative to its bone through `offset`, since a direct write to the `Transform` is overwritten at the next Attach. Any field may be edited at any time; the bone is looked up again by engine name whenever the skeleton entity, the name or the skeleton's instance changes. `Skeletons::GetAttachmentState` reports whether it placed the entity, and why not.

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton entity: an entity with a `SkeletonPose`.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: The entity's place relative to the bone.

types.name: Fenrir::Channels
types.doc: Which parts of a bone's local transform a pose target writes: a mask, combined with `|`.

values.name: KeepLocal
values.doc: Removes the `BoneAttachment` only: the entity keeps its local `Transform` and its parent.

values.name: KeepWorld
values.doc: Reparents the entity, keeping where it is in the world now.

types.name: Fenrir::DetachResult
types.doc: What `Skeletons::Detach` did. Every result but `Detached` changed nothing.

values.name: NotAttached
values.doc: The entity is dead or has no `BoneAttachment`.

values.name: InsidePipeline
values.doc: Called while the pose pipeline runs, where structural changes are refused.

values.name: InvalidParent
values.doc: The new parent is dead, the entity itself or one of its descendants.

values.name: ParentNotInvertible
values.doc: The new parent's world matrix has no inverse.

values.name: NotRepresentable
values.doc: The world transform cannot be held as position, rotation and scale under the new parent (shear).

types.name: Fenrir::OverrideScope
types.doc: Which bones an override weight assignment reaches (ADR-0038).

values.name: Bone
values.doc: The bone alone.

values.name: BoneSubtree
values.doc: The bone and every bone below it, each given the value.

types.name: Fenrir::PoseKind
types.doc: Which of a skeleton's poses a base-pose read gives (ADR-0040).

values.name: Render
values.doc: The pose this frame draws, the render pose: the default.

values.name: Simulation
values.doc: The pose the last fixed tick evaluated, the simulation pose: the base pose at tick time, with no modifiers, so a world read of it is the bone's model matrix in that pose. On a frame-posed skeleton it is the render pose.

types.name: Fenrir::PoseSpace
types.doc: The space a pose target's transform is given in (ADR-0028, ADR-0033).

values.name: Local
values.doc: Relative to the bone's parent bone; for a root bone, to the skeleton entity.

values.name: Model
values.doc: Relative to the skeleton entity: model space, never including the entity's own `Transform`.

values.name: World
values.doc: The scene's world space.

types.name: Fenrir::PoseState
types.doc: Whether a skeleton entity's pose can be read (ADR-0031).

values.name: Ready
values.doc: Its skeleton asset resolves and its pose is built: reads give the current pose.

values.name: Unavailable
values.doc: Its `SkeletonPose` names an empty or stale skeleton: reads are empty until it resolves.

values.name: Missing
values.doc: It is dead, or has no `SkeletonPose`.

types.name: Fenrir::PoseTiming
types.doc: When a skeleton's base pose is evaluated (ADR-0040).

values.name: Frame
values.doc: Once a frame, in the frame pass of the pose pipeline: the default.

values.name: Tick
values.doc: Once per fixed tick, at tick time: a tick-posed skeleton, for bodies that follow its bones. Its base pose is evaluated by the tick pass of `Animate` in `PreTick`, giving the simulation pose, and the frame draws the last two ticks' blend at `Time::accumulator / Time::tickRate`, with modifiers on top: the render pose.

types.name: Fenrir::SkeletonPose
types.doc: The skeleton pose (ADR-0031): plain data on a skeleton entity, naming the skeleton asset its pose instances. One per entity. FenrirSkeleton keeps the pose itself (base and final locals, model matrices, the palette) in a private scene resource, made for the component when the pose pipeline next reconciles, or at once by `Skeletons::Ensure`. Changing `skeleton` rebuilds the instance at the rest pose; switching `timing` is a field edit, taking effect at the next pass's reconcile. Switching to `Tick` seeds both tick poses with the current base pose, so nothing jumps; switching back to `Frame` resumes frame `Animate` from where the tick clock stopped.

fields.name: skeleton
fields.doc: The skeleton asset this instance poses. Empty or stale, the instance is `Unavailable`.

fields.name: timing
fields.doc: When its base pose is evaluated.

types.name: Fenrir::Target
types.doc: A pose target (ADR-0033): one write a pose modifier makes to a bone. It is resolved into the bone's local transform when written, and blended into it by `weight` for the masked channels (translation and scale lerp, rotation nlerps along the shortest arc). It is met when written, not held against later moves of the bone's ancestors.

fields.name: trs
fields.doc: The transform the bone should have, in `space`.

fields.name: channels
fields.doc: The channels written; the others keep the bone's current local values.

fields.name: weight
fields.doc: How far towards `trs` the bone moves, clamped to [0, 1]: 0 writes nothing, 1 writes it exactly.
